summary: Rabbi Harari explores whether the obligation to wear special clothing on Shabbat extends to one's shoes. He examines various sources from the Gemara and later authorities that debate whether shoes are considered distinct from clothing, ultimately concluding that while having separate Shabbat shoes is a midat hasidut, it is not an absolute necessity. He suggests that polishing one's weekday shoes for Shabbat can serve as a way to honor the day.
questions: Is there an obligation to wear special shoes for Shabbat just like we wear special clothing?
Do the Berakhot we say in the morning imply that shoes and clothing are separate categories?
Can I use my fancy weekday shoes for Shabbat if I polish them?
What does it mean to have a midat hasidut regarding Shabbat footwear?
